decisions.1_sourceOfTruth: packages/design-system theme is canonical. src/cobranding (baseThemes.ts, createPartnerTheme.ts) is partner navigation chrome only and is out of scope.
decisions.2_fractionalValues: Bind Figma to the INTENDED integer, record the true computed value alongside as 'computedPx'. Never emit a fractional value into Figma.
decisions.3_buttonLargeFontSize: Transcribe the real 15px and flag it. Tebra overrides sizeSmall only, so size=large inherits MUI's 15px font against Tebra's 24px line-height.
decisions.4_autocompleteScope: Build the full component with a provenance split: every value carries layer='tebra' or layer='mui-substrate' so the unthemed surface is visible rather than silently canonized.

pxToRemHazard.explanation: MUI computes coef = typography.fontSize / 14, then pxToRem(size) = size / htmlFontSize * coef. typography.ts sets fontSize: 16 and htmlFontSize: 16, so coef = 1.1428571428571428 and EVERY pxToRem call in the theme and in MUI's own component sources is inflated by 14.29%.

geometry._paddingConvention: Contained variants carry a 1px border that CSS adds to the auto height. Figma padding = CSS padding + 1 with an INSIDE stroke reproduces the exact outer box with integer values. Text variants have no border, so padding is the CSS padding verbatim.

iconPaddingPull._rule: When Start icon is on, reduce paddingLeft by the pull. When End icon is on, reduce paddingRight by the pull.

TextField.layer: UNTHEMED MUI SUBSTRATE — the strongest example in the library
TextField.provenanceHeadline: TextFieldOverrides.tsx contains NO styleOverrides. Its entire content is one defaultProp swapping the Select dropdown icon for a grey DownCaret. No MuiOutlinedInput, MuiInputBase, MuiInputLabel, MuiFormControl or MuiFormHelperText override exists anywhere in the theme. Outline, padding, radius, label float, notch and helper text are MUI v5.15.12 as shipped; only the palette values flowing through them are Tebra.

argTypes._finding: The story declares exactly ONE argType: margin. There is no size, variant or state argType. Axes were derived from the story args and the TextFieldVariations examples, not assumed.

sizeAxisProvenance._status: THE ONE DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION to the 'stories are the structure source' rule

An earlier build kept it in flow, which let the 28px clear indicator inflate the field to 60/44 — in CSS the absolute adornment can never affect height.

PrimaryNavBar._status: BUILT and CLOSED 2026-08-03. Tebra-default partner theme only. Geometry settled by design ruling against the rendered product; no further nav passes without a new product screenshot showing a delta. Not canonical design-system truth; publish gated.
PrimaryNavBar._scopeFinding: The primary nav bar never renders under the canonical design-system theme. navigation-ui/src/root.component.tsx:37 mounts <CobrandedApp />, which wraps the whole nav in <ThemeProvider theme={createPartnerTheme(partnerId)}> — and the default is createPartnerTheme('tebra'), not the design-system theme. So the nav is governed entirely by src/cobranding, which schema.decisions.1_sourceOfTruth already declares out of scope: 'src/cobranding is partner navigation chrome only and is out of scope.' Building a nav bar in the Figma library would mean either bringing cobranding into scope or documenting a surface the canonical theme does not control. That is Daniel's call, not a build decision.
PrimaryNavBar._nearMiss: Worth knowing before re-deriving this: reading Navigation.tsx and NavIconButton.tsx alone produces a false accessibility defect. NavIconButton forces color: primary.contrastText (#fff) and swaps the background to action.hover on hover. Under the CANONICAL theme action.hover is #CBDDE0 (Growth 4, opaque), which would put white on a pale ground at about 1.4:1. That never happens, because createPartnerTheme remaps action.hover to navIconHoverBackground = #195b63, giving roughly 7.7:1. The bug only exists if you stop reading before the ThemeProvider. This is the 'the theme is the component' rule biting one level further out than usual — the nav has its OWN theme.

(1) It recorded the bar as 64px and dismissed the legacy library's 65px as a legacy-only value. WRONG: createPartnerTheme.ts sets MuiIconButton.styleOverrides.sizeLarge to height 65px / width 65px, and Navigation.tsx's sx minHeight:64 is a FLOOR, not a fixed height — so the 65px icon buttons expand the Toolbar and the bar RENDERS at 65px. geometryRuling.source: Daniel, design authority — product-rendered authority for the nav surface.
geometryRuling.ruling: THE RENDERED PRODUCT IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR NAV GEOMETRY. The bar is 65px. The search field centres within it at its natural height (~45px).
geometryRuling.whyTheDerivationWasWrong: The 76.8px figure was CSS arithmetic that never renders. It summed the search wrapper's Box p:2 (32px) onto the 44.8px field as if the toolbar stacked paddings. A flex toolbar with align-items:center CENTRES its children — it does not sum their box heights into its own. The 44.8px field inside a 32px-padded wrapper centres in whatever height the toolbar actually is; it does not push the toolbar to 76.8. minHeight:64 plus the 65x65 sizeLarge icon buttons is what sets the height, and that is 65.
geometryRuling.derivationChain: 64 -> 65 -> 76.8 -> 65. Three passes each produced a different number from the same source, and only the last matches the product. Recorded as the reason arithmetic is not trusted for this surface: every step was individually defensible and the chain still landed wrong.
alsoRuled: Selected/active slot wash is BUILT even though source has no distinct selected state. Designers have to mock active navigation; the code conflating hover and active is a finding to record, not a reason to omit the state. Selected paints identically to Hover because that is what the code does.
Where source-derivation and rendered product disagree on this surface, match the product wholesale.

That fixed box was the stray wide frame producing the empty gap between the practice name and the search.

flags.summary: Paint-level opacity on a variable-bound paint does not propagate to INSTANCES. Masters render correctly; every instance renders at full opacity.
flags.detail: Known already: structural operations discard paint-level opacity, so it must be applied last. NEW and worse: even when the master reads the correct opacity, a freshly created instance reads 1. Verified on Table / Row State=Selected — master 0.08, instance 1 — and confirmed unfixable by re-creating the instance or by resetOverrides.
flags.fix: Put the alpha in the VARIABLE instead of the paint. A variable whose stored value carries its own alpha channel propagates to instances correctly. Demonstrated with color/computed (no palette)/rowSelected = rgba(0,72,82,0.08): master 0.08, instance 0.08, still bound, still zero unbound paints.
knownAffected: Chip — 18 alpha paints: Default/Hover at action.selected 12%, Outlined Secondary and Warning borders at 70% and their 4% hovers. Masters correct, instances will render solid.
Checkbox, Radio — hover ripple halos at alpha(primary.main, 0.04).
Alert, Menu, Autocomplete — no paint-level alpha; these use variables that already carry their own alpha (action.disabled, substrate/inputOutline) and are NOT affected.
flags.status: CLOSED 2026-08-02 by the alpha-to-variable remediation pass — see remediation below.

remediation.sweep: File-wide enumeration rather than the known list: 48 paints across 12 distinct (variable, opacity) combinations. The known list was INCOMPLETE — outlined Chip borders at 70% exist for error, info and success as well as secondary and warning, and the Dialog reference frame's scrim at 50% was unlisted.
remediation.namingRule: Named for the FORMULA — which colour at what alpha — not for the consuming component. alphaPrimary04 is shared by Checkbox, Radio and Switch: Switch's rule is alpha(action.active, 0.04) and the others use alpha(primary.main, 0.04), and paletteValues.ts gives both the same literal #004852. The variable description records that if those two palette entries ever diverge, this variable must split.
remediation.instanceVerification: 49 instance paints checked by instantiating every affected variant and comparing the RENDERED paint — colour, effective alpha and bound variable — against its master. 0 mismatches. Master-level reads were explicitly not accepted as evidence.
remediation.alsoFound: The widened audit surfaced 3 unbound paints that every previous audit had missed, in the Radio DO NOT USE reference frame's orphan glyph. Prior audits walked component sets only, never reference frames. Both the paints and the audit scope are fixed.

flags.whyItWasMissed: Every prior audit measured MASTERS. Reference frames built from instances existed for Menu, Radio, Button group and Dialog, but none of those used a paint-level alpha, so the divergence never rendered until the Table reference frame put an alpha row in an instance.

flags.summary: Four selectable row surfaces, two different selected treatments — the split is now 2 vs 2.

A product showing a table and a menu side by side shows two different selection languages.
flags.handling: All four built as they resolve. Reported, not normalised.

flags.summary: PaginationOverrides is the only thing Tebra changes about Pagination, and it changes selected from a pale wash to solid teal.

The circular shape (borderRadius = height/2) is NOT overridden and survives. Arrows are MUI's own NavigateBefore/NavigateNext — the coverage sweep expected Tebra's LeftCaret to ride along here, which was wrong; PaginationOverrides sets no slots.
flags.notBuilt: The selected:hover cell — the State axis carries Default/Hover/Selected/Disabled with no selected-hover combination.

flags.summary: TablePagination's rows-per-page select is a STANDARD-variant Select and cannot reuse the built Text field Select.
flags.detail: TablePagination renders Select with variant='standard' — no outline, no notch, no 56px box. Text field's Select boolean is the outlined path: a 4px notched border at 56px tall. Reusing the built component would impose an outline and more than double the height inside a 52px toolbar.
flags.alsoFound: TablePaginationOverrides does NOT pin rowsPerPageOptions as the coverage sweep assumed. Its entire content is a SelectProps.IconComponent replacement — Tebra's DownCaretIcon at fontSize='xxsmall' (12px), absolutely positioned at right 0.4rem. That is a THIRD percentage/absolute caret construction after TextField's right:4% and Autocomplete's right:9.

flags.summary: The default chip's clickable hover resolves to a 12%-opacity ghost, near-invisible in the product.
flags.detail: MUI's clickable default-colour hover is alpha(action.selected, selectedOpacity 0.08 + hoverOpacity 0.04) = 12%. That formula assumes a translucent chip base, which is true of stock MUI where the default chip background is itself an alpha. Tebra's action.selected is a SOLID #F0EEE8, so applying 12% to it produces an almost imperceptible wash rather than a state change.
flags.handling: Built faithfully at 12% and a KNOWN ISSUE note added to all four Default/Hover variant descriptions so reviewers do not report it as a build error. Faithful in Figma, broken in code.

flags.summary: The success hover binding to success.light is correct — ChipOverrides defines its own clickable hover, overriding MUI's [color].dark rule.
flags.detail: ChipOverrides.colorSuccess contains '&.MuiChip-clickable': { '&:hover, &:active': { backgroundColor: theme.palette.success.light } }. Same pattern for colorInfo (primary[200]) and colorError (#FD919F). colorWarning does NOT define one, so warning falls through to MUI's palette.warning.dark #F2BA2A — which is what the build binds. No correction needed.

flags.summary: DialogTitle renders Typography variant='h6', and typography.ts defines no h6.
flags.detail: The Tebra ramp is h1-h5, subtitle2, body1, body2, button, caption. There is no h6, so DialogTitle falls back to MUI's own h6: pxToRem(20) — which under Tebra's inflated coef renders 22.86px, not 20 — at fontWeightMedium 500, a weight Akkurat LL cannot supply. Every dialog title in the product is therefore typeset off-ramp.
flags.handling: Built at the intended 20px in Akkurat Regular. Flagged as a ramp gap: either typography.ts gains an h6 or DialogTitle should be given a variant that exists.

flags.summary: Dialog actions are right-aligned by MUI itself, not by Tebra — unlike Card actions.
flags.detail: DialogActions ships justifyContent: flex-end in MUI 5.15.12. CardActions ships flex-start in MUI and is flipped to flex-end by CardActionsOverrides. The two surfaces look alike for opposite reasons, and only one of them would follow a Tebra decision to change.
flags.handling: Both built right-aligned with the provenance distinguished in each description.

flags.summary: The Drawer story uses variant='persistent', which is the docked path — no elevation, no backdrop.
flags.detail: MUI's Drawer defaults to variant='temporary' at elevation 16, but the story renders variant='persistent' anchor='right'. Persistent and permanent drawers are not Modals: they get no scrim, no elevation, and instead a 1px divider border on the side facing the content (borderLeft for a right anchor).
flags.handling: Built as docked with a left border. Elevation / 16 was NOT created — the ramp only carries steps a component actually reaches. If a temporary drawer ever ships, that step gets added then.

flags.summary: The three selectable list rows in this library resolve hover and selected three different ways.

List / Item.hover: action.hover #CBDDE0 — ListItemOverrides root, applied to EVERY ListItem whether interactive or not
List / Item.selected: NOT overridden — falls through to MUI's alpha(primary.main, 0.08), a translucent teal
List / Item.note: The List story exercises neither selected nor disabled, so only Default and Hover are built.

Menu / Item.hover: action.hover #CBDDE0 — MUI's own rule resolving to a Tebra value
Menu / Item.selected: action.selected #F0EEE8 — flat, MenuItemOverrides overriding MUI's alpha blend

Autocomplete / Option.selected: action.selected #F0EEE8 — flat, AutocompleteOverrides overriding MUI's alpha blend
Autocomplete / Option.selectedFocused: action.selected #F0EEE8 — Tebra flattens MUI's additive selected+hover

table.agreement: All three agree on hover (#CBDDE0). Menu and Autocomplete agree on a flat selected (#F0EEE8) but disagree on the selected+interaction state — Menu goes to hover, Autocomplete stays at selected. List agrees with neither on selected, because it has no selected override at all and keeps MUI's translucent alpha(primary.main, 0.08).

flags.handling: All three built as they resolve. Reported, not normalised — a shared list-row treatment would be a code decision across three override files.

flags.summary: Five interactive surfaces from the same ButtonBase lineage, five different treatments — and one that ships disabled.

Radio.hover: MUI 4% ripple circle, 42px — present only because RadioButtonOverrides never executes

IconButton.hover: SOLID action.hover #CBDDE0 — Tebra root override replaces MUI's 4% tint

CardActionArea.hover: NONE REACHABLE — CardActionAreaOverrides sets defaultProps disabled: true, so the ripple surface ships disabled

Any consumer wanting a clickable card must pass disabled={false} explicitly. This is open decision 4 from the Known drift record, now confirmed at source.
flags.handling: Card built without a CardActionArea axis; the reason is recorded in the component description.

flags.summary: CardActionsOverrides sets justifyContent: flex-end — MUI defaults to flex-start.
flags.detail: The only content of CardActionsOverrides. Card actions are right-aligned throughout the library where MUI would left-align them.
flags.handling: Built as resolved.

flags.summary: The Accordion expand caret is forced black with htmlColor, a literal rather than a token.
flags.detail: AccordionSummaryOverrides sets expandIcon to <DownCaretIcon fontSize="small" htmlColor="black" />. htmlColor bypasses the palette entirely — the CSS keyword 'black' happens to equal text.primary #000000, so it is not visually wrong today, but it is unthemed and would not follow a palette change.
flags.handling: Bound to color/common/black in Figma, which matches the literal. Flagged as a token-governance item rather than a visual defect.

flags.status: NOT APPLIED — reporting rather than absorbing, per instruction
flags.summary: Neither approved retrofit is a clean instance swap. Both would change rendered geometry, so neither was applied.

autocomplete.finding: The Autocomplete indicators ARE IconButtons in code, but they are styled(IconButton) wrappers that override padding: AutocompletePopupIndicator sets padding 2 and AutocompleteClearIndicator sets padding 4, against IconButton's own padding 8.
autocomplete.consequence: Figma cannot override padding on an instance — padding is not a component property — so an IconButton instance would impose 34 or 40 px where the code renders 24 and 28. The end adornment is a fixed 52x28 absolute box; a 40px child would overflow it and the 56/40 field heights would no longer hold.
options: leave the indicators as purpose-built constructions (current state, geometry correct)
add Size variants to Icon button matching the Autocomplete paddings (2 and 4), which would invent sizes the IconButton story never exercises
expose padding as a variable-bound property, which Figma does not support for instances

alert.finding: Alert's close IS a plain IconButton — AlertActions.example.tsx renders <IconButton color="inherit" size="small"> around <CloseOutlinedIcon fontSize="xxsmall"> — but two things do not line up.
alert.consequence: The code's box is 8 + 12 + 8 = 28px because the icon is xxsmall (0.75rem = 12px); the built Icon button Small is 34px because its glyph is MUI's sizeSmall 18px. Swapping would grow the slot by 6px. Separately, color='inherit' is not on the Icon button Color axis at all — the IconButton story's argTypes offer only default, primary and error.
options: add Color=Inherit to Icon button (justified by AlertActions usage, the same class of justification as Menu) and accept the 6px growth
add an icon-size property to Icon button

flags.recommendation: Leave both as-is until the Icon button axes are deliberately extended. The current constructions are geometrically correct against source; the retrofit would trade correct pixels for nominal reuse.

flags.summary: IconButtonOverrides.sizeSmall sets padding to 0.5rem = 8px, the same as medium, so small and medium differ only by icon size.
flags.detail: MUI's sizeSmall is padding 5 with an 18px icon, giving a 28px box. Tebra's override raises the padding to 8, giving 34px against medium's 40px. The touch target grows by 6px and the two sizes stop being visually distinct at the box level.
flags.handling: Built as resolved: 34px small, 40px medium. This is also why the Alert close retrofit does not line up — see iconButtonRetrofitBlocked.

flags.summary: IconButton, Checkbox and Radio each use a different disabled colour, and IconButton's hover is solid where the others are a 4% tint.

disabled.Radio: action.disabled rgba(0,0,0,0.5) — substrate, because RadioButtonOverrides never executes

hover.IconButton: SOLID action.hover #CBDDE0 — the Tebra root override replaces MUI's alpha(action.active, 0.04)

flags.handling: All built as they ship. Four sibling controls from the same lineage, four disabled treatments and two hover models. Reported, not harmonised.

flags.summary: There is no PaperOverrides in this codebase; the old app-build audit's 'rounded 8' does not apply here.
flags.detail: No file in src/overrides registers MuiPaper, so Paper takes shape.borderRadius = 4. Every Paper-derived surface already built — Menu, Snackbar, Alert, Autocomplete's listbox — is therefore correct at 4.
flags.handling: Paper built at 4 with a Square axis for the story's `variant='outlined' square` usage.

flags.summary: MUI draws Link's underline at alpha(primary.main, 0.4); Figma cannot colour a text decoration separately from its glyphs.
flags.detail: MUI Link with the default underline='always' sets textDecorationColor to a 40% tint of the link colour, so the rule is visibly lighter than the text. Figma's textDecoration is a boolean on the text node and inherits the fill.
flags.handling: Underline renders at full strength, documented as a deviation in the component description.

flags.summary: The premise that Alert's four severity backgrounds are MUI-computed tints does not hold for anything the story exercises.
flags.detail: MUI computes a standard tint as lighten(palette[severity].light, 0.9) with text darken(light, 0.6). But AlertOverrides.tsx exists and replaces standardInfo, standardWarning and standardError with background.paper (#FFFFFF) plus a 1px coloured border. The one severity that would keep its computed tint is standardSuccess — and the story's severity argType is [error, info, warning], with no success. Outlined, which is entirely computed, is likewise absent from the variant argType [filled, standard]. So ZERO computed tints are reachable through the built surface.
flags.whatWouldHaveBeen: standardSuccess would be lighten(#6FC691, 0.9) ≈ #F1F9F4 on darken(#6FC691, 0.6) ≈ #2C4F3A text with a success.main icon. Recorded here rather than built, because the story does not offer it.
flags.handling: No tint variables created for standard. The only computed value that IS reachable is filled warning's text — see alertFilledWarningTextComputed.

flags.summary: Filled warning's text is a computed contrast value with no palette entry.
flags.detail: MUI Alert filled sets color: getContrastText(palette[severity].main). warning.main #FCDE73 has roughly a 1.3 contrast ratio against white, below the 3.0 contrastThreshold, so getContrastText returns MUI's internal light.text.primary = rgba(0,0,0,0.87) — NOT Tebra's text.primary #000. Filled info (#4678CC) and filled error (#D83B4D) both clear the threshold and resolve to #FFFFFF.
flags.handling: Bound to color/computed (no palette)/alertFilledWarningText, with the computation recorded in the variable description. Renders on the Tokens page in the computed group with a literal rgba() code syntax.

flags.summary: The warning severity uses two unrelated hues depending on variant: coral in standard, yellow in filled.
flags.detail: AlertOverrides.standardWarning sets border and icon colour to secondary.main #FF8D6E — the coral brand colour — rather than warning.main. Filled warning has no Tebra override, so it takes MUI's palette.warning.main #FCDE73, a yellow. The same severity therefore reads coral as an inline alert and yellow as a banner.
flags.handling: Both built as resolved and visible side by side in the variant grid. Reported, not harmonised.

flags.summary: AttentionFilledIcon.tsx and InfoFilledIcon.tsx contain byte-identical paths, so error and info alerts render the same glyph.
flags.detail: Both draw a filled circle with an exclamation mark. AlertOverrides.iconMapping maps error to Attention and info to Info, so the two severities differ only by colour, never by shape. There is also no success entry in the mapping, so a success alert would fall back to MUI's own SuccessOutlinedIcon.
flags.handling: Both icon components created with the duplication noted in each description.

flags.summary: CORRECTION: SnackbarContent is not grey[900] #2B2B2B. It is info.dark #004852, or success.dark #2B865A.
flags.detail: SnackbarContentOverrides.ts sets backgroundColor to ownerState.type === 'success' ? success.dark : info.dark. `type` is a CUSTOM prop the theme reads off ownerState — it is not a standard MUI SnackbarContent prop, so it only takes effect when a consumer passes it. MUI's own computed background, emphasize(background.default, 0.8) ≈ #2E2E2D, is fully replaced. Text remains #FFFFFF because the base styled() derives colour from getContrastText of MUI's computed dark background, and the override touches only the background.
flags.handling: Built with a Type=Default|Success axis. Required adding color/info/dark, which the first variable pass had skipped because it duplicates primary.main.

flags.summary: CORRECTION: there is no TooltipOverrides. Tooltip is pure MUI substrate, and its grey exists nowhere in the Tebra palette.
flags.detail: The overrides index has no MuiTooltip entry. MUI sets backgroundColor: alpha(palette.grey[700], 0.92). paletteValues.ts defines grey 300/400/500/600/900 but NOT 700, and createPalette deepmerges the partial ramp onto MUI's default grey, so grey[700] stays #616161. The tooltip therefore renders rgba(97,97,97,0.92) — a grey with no Tebra provenance at all.
flags.handling: Bound to color/computed (no palette)/tooltipBackground. Typography is substrate too: pxToRem(11) bound to the intended 11, and fontWeightMedium 500 which Akkurat LL cannot supply, so it ships Regular.

flags.summary: The two dark feedback surfaces disagree on everything except their white text.
flags.detail: Snackbar is #004852 teal at typography body2 (14/20) with radius 4, padding 6/16, elevation 6, from a Tebra override. Tooltip is rgba(97,97,97,0.92) grey at 11px weight-500 with radius 4, padding 4/8, no elevation, entirely from MUI. They share only white text and the 4px radius. There is no single dark-surface treatment in this library — one is branded, the other is whatever MUI shipped.
flags.handling: Both built as they ship, with the disagreement stated in each description and here.

flags.summary: Segments built as a Position=First|Middle|Last axis composed in an auto-layout row, not as fixed composites per segment count.
flags.why: MUI composes positionally — it assigns firstButton / middleButton / lastButton classes by child index and drives all the radius and seam CSS off those classes. A Position axis is the same model, and it lets designers add or remove segments freely; the story alone uses both 2-segment and 3-segment groups, so a fixed composite per count would have needed two components on day one.
flags.tradeoff: Figma cannot assign a variant property by child index. A designer who inserts or reorders a segment must update Position by hand, and a wrong Position puts the seam and the pill cap in the wrong place. A fixed composite would have made that impossible but would not scale past the counts shipped.
flags.reuse: Every one of the 54 segments is a CLONE of the corresponding Variant=Contained Button variant, so padding, typography, label, icon slots and state colours are Button's validated internals rather than redrawn rectangles.

flags.summary: Contained groups get NO negative margin, so the join is two full 1px borders; Tebra resolves it differently per colour.
flags.detail: MUI's marginLeft: -1 seam collapse is scoped to `variant === 'outlined'` only (ButtonGroup.js lastButton/middleButton block). Tebra's ButtonGroupOverrides sets defaultProps variant 'contained', so no group in this library gets the collapse — adjacent segments sit flush and the join is the left segment's right border plus the right segment's left border.

resolved.primary: groupedContainedPrimary sets `&:not(:last-of-type) { borderColor: core.main; borderRightColor: transparent }` — the left segment's right border disappears, leaving the next segment's core.main left border as a single 1px sage line.
resolved.secondary: groupedContainedSecondary sets `&:not(:last-of-type) { borderColor: secondary.main; borderRightColor: primary.main }` — a teal right border against the next segment's coral left border, reading as a 1px teal divider. Drawn in Figma as a 1px Seam rectangle, because Figma cannot colour one side of a stroke independently.
resolved.disabledNonLast: groupedContainedHorizontal's `&:not(:last-child):disabled { borderRightColor: transparent }` carries higher specificity than groupedContainedPrimary's `&:disabled { borderColor: core.main }`, so the right border stays transparent. For secondary, groupedContainedSecondary resolves last in the overridesResolver and sets borderRightColor primary[200], which wins.

flags.radii: Button's radius 24 is kept on the outer ends only: first loses its right radii, last its left, middle all four. 24 still clamps to height/2, so end caps read as pill halves at 15 / 19 / 21. Tebra does not override the group radius; ButtonGroupRoot's own shape.borderRadius 4 is invisible because the container has no fill or border.

flags.summary: A disabled primary segment has a core.main border; a standalone disabled contained-primary Button has a primary[100] border.
flags.detail: ButtonOverrides.containedPrimary sets `&.Mui-disabled { border: 1px solid primary[100] }` (#CBDDE0). ButtonGroupOverrides.groupedContainedPrimary sets `&:disabled { borderColor: core.main }` (#B3C6C4), and group styles resolve after the button's own. So the same button looks different inside a group — a visibly darker disabled outline.
flags.handling: Built as resolved, visible in the assembled disabled example. Reported, not harmonised.

flags.summary: A non-last primary segment's hover binds primary[100]; a standalone Button's hover binds action.hover. Both are #CBDDE0.
flags.detail: groupedContainedPrimary sets `&:not(:last-of-type) { &:hover, &:active { backgroundColor: primary[100] } }` while ButtonOverrides.containedPrimary uses action.hover. paletteValues.ts gives both the same literal, so there is no visual difference today — but the two would diverge the moment either token changes.
flags.handling: Segments bind the token the group override names, so the Figma binding matches the code path rather than the coincidence.

flags.summary: No Variant and no orientation axis: the story never sets either, and the theme constrains both.
flags.detail: ButtonGroupOverrides.defaultProps pins variant to 'contained' (MUI's default is 'outlined'), and the story never passes variant or orientation. theme.ts's ButtonGroupPropsColorOverrides also disables inherit, success, error, info and warning, leaving primary and secondary — exactly the two the story's color argType offers. Size IS exercised (small/medium/large) so it is built.
flags.handling: Colour axis limited to Primary and Secondary per the type augmentation, matching the story.

flags.summary: Chip gained Size=Medium|Small for parity with Autocomplete / Tag, doubling the set to 84 variants.
flags.provenance: Same treatment as Text field's Size axis: the capability exists in code (MUI supports size on Chip, and Autocomplete already passes it through to Tag) but the Chip story never exercises it. Built for library parity, not because the story shows it — the third documented exception to structure-from-argTypes.
flags.geometry: Reused from the validated Tag derivation: height 24, radius 24/2 = 12, fontSize pxToRem(12) bound to 12, deleteIcon 16, ChipLabel small padding 8 filled / 7 outlined, itemSpacing 4 / 3 from deleteIcon small marginLeft -4. Medium ordered first so the variant default resolves to the code default.
flags.note: Cloning inside the set dropped all componentPropertyReferences again; 84 were mirrored back from the Medium half and verified at 2 per variant.

flags.summary: The two ChipOverrides literals are now variables in a separated 'hardcoded (no palette)' group, so the token layer shows them as the orphans they are.

color/hardcoded (no palette)/chipSuccess.reachedBy: any color='success' Chip — the story's Status Chip row renders it

color/hardcoded (no palette)/chipErrorCl.reason: needs color='error' AND clickable together; no story combines them
color/hardcoded (no palette)/chipErrorCl.builtAsVariant: yes, but only as a by-product of a uniform State axis — see handling

flags.codeSyntaxIsALiteral: Both carry their raw hex as WEB code syntax instead of var(--...), because there is no CSS variable to point at. On the Tokens page that renders as a bare hex among 46 var() entries, which is the intended tell.
flags.handling: One value is story-reachable and one is not. Rather than break the State axis, Chip carries Hover for all seven colours uniformly, so Error+Hover exists and is the only place #FD919F renders. Flagged here as unreachable in current product usage — a strict reading of 'do not build unreachable variants' would have left a hole in the axis, which is worse for a component set.

flags.summary: Tebra's per-colour Chip overrides land after MUI's outlined transparency and win, so outlined success/info/error chips are NOT transparent.
flags.detail: MUI's base styled() sets `variant outlined -> backgroundColor: transparent`. ChipOverrides colorSuccess / colorInfo / colorError each set a backgroundColor, and theme styleOverrides are appended after the base, with styles[colorX] applying regardless of variant. Result: outlined success = #C3E7C0 fill + a 70% success border; outlined info = core.light fill; outlined error = error.light fill. Outlined warning IS transparent, because colorWarning sets only `color`, not a background. Outlined primary is white, because outlinedPrimary sets it explicitly and resolves last.
flags.handling: Built as resolved. Verified visually across all 14 variant/colour combinations.

flags.summary: A filled primary Chip's clickable hover is visually identical to its rest state.
flags.detail: MUI's clickable coloured hover is palette[color].dark. paletteValues.ts sets primary.dark = primary.main = #004852, so the hover produces no change. Same root cause as the palette entry itself — primary.dark is not a distinct value.
flags.handling: Both variants built; they render the same. Reported rather than invented around.

flags.summary: Standalone Chip has no Size axis; Autocomplete / Tag has one. Same underlying MUI component.
flags.detail: The Chip story declares only color and variant argTypes and never exercises size. Tag gets Size because Autocomplete passes `size` through to its chips (verified at Autocomplete.js:502-505). Small chip geometry is already validated on Tag: height 24, radius 12, font 12, delete icon 16, label padding 7.
flags.handling: Not built, per structure-from-argTypes. Cheap to add before publish and breaking after — the same call Daniel made for TextField's Size.

flags.summary: CORRECTION: I reported that `<Menu>` appears zero times in the library. That was wrong — it appears twice.

Both real usages open as `<Menu\n`: Button/Prepopulate.example.tsx:32 and Chip/DropChip.pattern.stories.tsx:87. The standalone `<Select>` claim re-checked clean — it genuinely appears zero times.
consequences: Menu IS directly exercised, not only reached through <TextField select>. The Menu / Item and Menu components are better justified than the original note claimed, and Menu is not a structure-from-argTypes exception in the way Select is.

Elevation is NOT always 8: Prepopulate passes elevation={1} explicitly. The Menu composite's Elevation / 8 style represents Menu's default; an Elevation / 1 variant of the composite is a legitimate addition.
Anchoring is not universal: Prepopulate uses anchorOrigin bottom-right / transformOrigin top-right. The no-gap bottom-left offset on the reference frame is Menu's default only.

MenuItem content: Chip.stories.tsx:266 puts a <ListItemText primary={...}> inside a MenuItem. Still a single text line with no icon and no secondary line, so the 'no icon or secondary-text slots' decision stands, but it is not literally 'plain text' everywhere.

flags.partiallyCorrectedBy: menuUsageClaimWasWrong — the '<Menu> appears zero times' half of this was wrong
flags.summary: There is no Select story and no Menu story folder. Standalone `<Select>` appears zero times; `<Menu>` appears twice, in two pattern stories (see correction).
flags.detail: Every dropdown in this design system is `<TextField select>`. MenuItem appears only as its children — Drawer.example (13), TextField.stories (7), AccordionDetails.example (7), FormDialog.example (5), DropChip.pattern (5), Chip.stories (3), Prepopulate.pattern (3). MUI renders that as Select -> Menu -> Popover Paper -> MenuList -> MenuItem, so the parts are real and shipping even though no story exercises them directly.
flags.handling: No standalone Select component was built — it would duplicate Text field's Select boolean, which already IS the closed control. Menu / Item and Menu were built, sourced from MenuItemOverrides plus MUI substrate rather than from a story. This is the second documented exception to structure-from-argTypes, after TextField's Size axis.

flags.summary: MUI's Select diverges from a plain outlined TextField in three ways, and Tebra's icon replacement adds a fourth.

divergences.detail: nativeSelectSelectStyles gives the outlined select element paddingRight: 32, overriding OutlinedInput's input padding of 14, to reserve space for the icon. Text field's Select boolean cannot vary padding by boolean, so its text clearance stays 14 — the same limitation class as Button's icon padding pull.

MUI places the select icon at right: 7 with color action.active and top: calc(50% - .5em). Tebra replaces the icon component wholesale via TextFieldOverrides SelectProps.IconComponent, so none of that applies: the Tebra caret uses right: 4%, color grey[600], top: calc(50% - 12px).

right: '4%' is a PERCENTAGE, so the inset scales with field width. Figma cannot express a percentage inset. Modelled at a stated reference width of 300px, where 4% = 12px. At 600px the real caret sits 24px in; at 200px, 8px. MUI's own 7px would have been width-independent.

MUI's select icon rotates 180 degrees when open (`ownerState.open && { transform: 'rotate(180deg)' }` in nativeSelectIconStyles). Tebra's replacement is a plain styled(DownCaretIcon) that never receives ownerState, so THE TEBRA SELECT CARET DOES NOT ROTATE WHEN THE MENU OPENS. Autocomplete's popup indicator does rotate, because AutocompletePopupIndicator handles it. The two dropdowns in this library behave differently on open.

flags.handling: All four transcribed into the Text field description and here. No Open axis was built on the closed control, because with a non-rotating caret there is no visual difference between open and closed.

flags.summary: The Menu's list padding is 0, not MUI's 8 — and it disagrees with the Autocomplete listbox.
flags.detail: ListOverrides.ts sets MuiList defaultProps disablePadding: true globally. MenuList renders a List, so the Menu paper has zero vertical list padding. The Autocomplete listbox is a styled div, not a List, so it keeps MUI's padding '8px 0'. Two dropdown surfaces in the same library, 8px apart.
flags.handling: Menu built with padding 0, Autocomplete listbox left at 8. Reported, not harmonised — the fix is a code decision.

flags.summary: Menu's elevation 8 shadow is pure MUI substrate — the Tebra theme never defines a shadows array.
flags.detail: createTheme is passed only palette, typography and components, so all 25 elevations are MUI defaults. Only three are actually reached by this library: 1 (Paper default, Autocomplete listbox), 3 (referenced directly by AlertOverrides), and 8 (Popover default, which Menu inherits). Nothing in the theme reviews or overrides any of them.
flags.handling: Elevation / 1, 3 and 8 created as bound effect styles translated layer-for-layer from theme.shadows. See figmaBuild.overlayRecipe.

flags.generator: tokens-page-generator.js, alongside this schema. THE GENERATOR NOW EXISTS ON DISK — it did not before 2026-08-03, which is the only reason the page was ever allowed to go stale. Five steps, each run as its own use_figma call: clear+header, colour, typography, dimension, verify. Only one value is hand-substituted (<DATE> in step 1); everything else is derived from the file.
flags.summary: The Tokens page is a generated, read-only rendering of the three variable collections. Do not hand-edit it.
flags.lastRegenerated: 2026-08-03 — full rebuild from the live collections after tier 6 left the page reporting 62 colour / 31 dimension against 67 / 32. Recovered the five missing swatches: illustrationTeal, illustrationCream, uaDefaultLinkBlue (hardcoded), alphaBlack04, alphaBlack12 (computed). illustrationTeal now renders #004952 in red in the hardcoded group, which is the whole reason that variable exists. The hardcoded group caption was corrected — it still claimed ChipOverrides.ts was the only source, which stopped being true when the illustrations landed.
flags.regenerate: Whenever any variable collection changes. Run the five steps in tokens-page-generator.js in order. The generator reads collections live via getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync / getLocalVariablesAsync and derives every swatch, specimen, bar, group membership, ordering and header count from them, so a regenerated page cannot drift from the variables. Hand edits will be destroyed on the next run — step 1 clears the page frame's children first.
flags.authoredNotDerived: Four things in the generator are authored constants rather than reads, and are the only places the page can go stale on its own: the colour GROUP_ORDER list, the two '(no palette)' group captions, the ALIASES map, and the typography blurb. A group not in GROUP_ORDER is appended last and REPORTED in the return value as unplacedGroups; a dimension prefix that is not space/radius/border/size is reported as unplaced. Neither is ever silently dropped.
flags.boundNotPainted: Swatch fills bind their own variable; spacing bar widths, component-size rule heights, corner radii and stroke weights all bind theirs (18 width + 7 height + 16 radius + 12 stroke-side bindings, 0 failures). Only values Figma cannot bind — hex strings, var() syntax, px numbers, brand aliases — are rendered as text. Verified 2026-08-03: 569 solid paints, 0 unbound; 0 fractional authored dimensions.
flags.aliasSource: Brand aliases (Growth 1, Vitality 0, Synapse ramp, Backbone, Core, Siren/First aid/Remedy, Energize/Neuron, Restore/Cyto/Vigor, Practice/Circadian) are transcribed from the trailing comments in paletteValues.ts. The generator keys them BY LITERAL, not by token name — that is how secondary/contrastText and core/contrastText, which carry no comment in source but hold #004852, resolve to 'Growth 1'. 41 of the 47 palette-group colours have an alias; the other 6 render without one because no commented literal matches. Note tokens.color['secondary.100'].tebraName in this schema reads 'vitality 4' while source reads 'vitality 4, used for disabled' and the page renders 'Vitality 4 (disabled)' — the schema copy is the abridged one.

flags.summary: Four variables carry no WEB code syntax. All four were added in tier 6; every variable created before then has one.
flags.detail: The two tier-4 hardcoded orphans (chipSuccessBackground, chipErrorClickableHover) deliberately carry their raw hex as WEB code syntax, so the token layer shows a bare literal among var() entries. The three tier-6 hardcoded colours carry nothing at all, and space/40 carries nothing while every other space token has var(--tebra-space-N).
flags.handling: NOT resolved unilaterally — setting a code syntax is a token-layer edit, and for space/40 the plausible value var(--tebra-space-40) would be invented rather than transcribed (see flags.tebraCssVarsDoNotExist). The generator renders the gap instead of hiding it: a colour with no code syntax falls back to its own hex literal in red, which is visually identical to the deliberate tier-4 convention; a dimension token with no code syntax renders 'no code syntax set' in red. So the page is honest either way.
flags.decisionNeeded: Daniel: set the three hardcoded colours to their hex literals to match the tier-4 convention, and decide whether space/40 should carry a var() at all.

flags.summary: The var(--tebra-*) code syntax on ~112 variables does not correspond to any CSS custom property in web-app-v2. Nothing in the source defines or reads those names.
flags.evidence: grep -rE '--tebra|cssVarPrefix|CssVarsProvider' over packages/design-system/src returns 0 matches; the same grep over the whole checkout returns 0 files. The theme is built with createTheme (not experimental_extendTheme / CssVarsProvider), so no CSS variables are emitted at all — emotion writes literal values into generated class names.
flags.impact: The code syntax is a Figma-side naming convention invented during this build, not a transcription from source. It reads as a promise that a developer can type var(--tebra-color-primary-main) and get the token; today they cannot. It also makes the flags.chipLiteralsBecameVariables phrasing — 'because there is no CSS variable to point at' — misleading, since it implies the other 112 do point at one.
flags.handling: Reported, not changed. This is a real disagreement between the Figma token layer and the code, which is the deliverable; it is not a bug to normalise. Options if it is ever resolved: strip the code syntax entirely, restate it as the JS path (theme.palette.primary.main), or ship the CSS variables in web-app-v2 and make it true. Do not quietly delete 112 code syntax entries.

flags.summary: RadioButtonOverrides.ts registers under the invalid key MuiRadioButton and has never executed. Radio ships raw MUI substrate.

intendedVsShipping.shipping: Hover renders MUI's ripple circle — alpha(primary.main, action.hoverOpacity 0.04) on the 42px SwitchBase, because Radio's ':hover' block is wrapped in `!ownerState.disableRipple &&`.
intendedVsShipping.intendedIfKeyFixed: The hover halo disappears entirely; the click ripple animation also stops. Nothing else changes — the override sets no colours, icons or geometry.
intendedVsShipping.acceptanceTest: The DO NOT USE reference frame on the Reference page shows both side by side and is the before/after test for the code fix.

flags.secondGap: components/icons/RadioCheckedIcon.tsx exists in the Tebra icon set but is referenced by nothing. It draws a filled disc with a white hole, unlike MUI's ring + dot that ships. A corrected MuiRadio key would NOT bring it in, because the override sets no icon props. Two separate gaps.

flags.summary: Checkbox and Radio use different disabled colours, purely because one override key is valid and the other is not.
flags.detail: Checkbox disabled comes from CheckboxOverrides.colorPrimary (a valid MuiCheckbox key): grey[400] #D6D6D6 unchecked, primary[100] #CBDDE0 checked/indeterminate. Radio disabled falls through to MUI's '&.Mui-disabled { color: action.disabled }', which Tebra sets to rgba(0,0,0,0.5) — a much darker, desaturated grey. Two controls that sit side by side in the same form disagree.
flags.handling: Both built as they ship. Reported rather than harmonised — resolving it is a code decision, and it is downstream of fixing the MuiRadioButton key.

flags.summary: The floating-label notch was faked with a background-coloured chip masking the border; rebuilt as a genuine gap in a three-slice outline.
flags.detail: MUI's NotchedOutline is a fieldset whose legend interrupts the top border. The original build simulated that with a background.paper-filled frame sitting on top of a stroked rectangle. That only reads correctly on white — on background.default #E8E5DF, cards, or the canvas it showed as a white chip floating on the border.

sourceGeometry.capLeftDerivation: NotchedOutlineRoot borderWidth 1 + padding '0 8px' -> the legend box starts 9px in
sourceGeometry.labelXAgreement: 9 + 5 = 14, which is exactly InputLabel's outlined shrunk transform translate(14px, -9px) — the two derivations agree independently
sourceGeometry.fieldsetTopOffset: top: -5 with legend height 11 — the legend straddles the border so the visible outline still lands on the input box at y=0. The -5 is the mechanism, not a different result; the 56px height is unaffected.

flags.handling: Rebuilt on all 10 Text field variants and all 30 Autocomplete / Field variants. Label slot hidden when the label does not float. The gap sizer is bound to the Label text property so the notch tracks custom labels. Verified on a background.default surface.

flags.summary: Both fields were filled with background.paper, but MUI's OutlinedInput declares no backgroundColor — the control is transparent.
flags.detail: OutlinedInputRoot sets position, borderRadius and border-colour rules only. Nothing paints a background. The paper fill was an unexamined assumption carried from the first build, and it is what let the fake notch look convincing.
flags.handling: Both Text field and Autocomplete / Field are now transparent, so the surface behind shows through the notch gap and the control body. Tag keeps its white fill, which IS Tebra (ChipOverrides.outlinedPrimary). Easily reverted if a filled input is wanted as a design decision, but it would be a decision, not a transcription.

flags.summary: The TextField story's two multiline examples are labelled backwards, and rows='grow' has no implementation anywhere in the checkout.
flags.detail: InputBase branches: `if (rows) { inputProps = {minRows: rows, maxRows: rows, ...} }` and BOTH branches then set InputComponent = TextareaAutosize. So `multiline` alone auto-grows, and `rows={n}` pins the height. The story labels the no-rows example 'Default Fixed Height in Rows' (it actually grows) and the rows='grow' example 'Original Multiline Height Behavior' (the string is fed into minRows/maxRows height arithmetic). grep for 'grow' across packages/design-system returns only the story itself — there is no patch implementing it.
flags.handling: RESOLVED as a process item — logged to the web-app-v2 bug list as item five (story documentation contradicts InputBase behaviour; the implied grow implementation does not exist in the checkout). The Figma model stays a static 3-row boolean, which is correct for a component library, and the component description states the real behaviour in one line so the story labels are not read as authoritative.

flags.status: RESOLVED — Size axis added for parity
flags.summary: The TextField story never exercises `size`, while Autocomplete / Field is built with Size=Medium|Small.
flags.detail: MUI supports size='small' on both components and both render at 40px. The Autocomplete story passes size through to its Chips; the TextField story declares only a margin argType and no size control.
flags.handling: Daniel's call: build the Size axis anyway for library parity, doubling the set to 20 variants, with the provenance stated explicitly in both the component description and components.TextField.figmaProperties.sizeAxisProvenance. This is the single documented exception to scoping structure from argTypes.

flags.summary: Cloning a variant that already lives inside a COMPONENT_SET silently drops every componentPropertyReferences on the clone and its descendants.
flags.detail: The 10 cloned Small variants had zero references while their Medium sources had 10 each. Nothing errors: setProperties on an instance still records the value, the variant just has no node listening, so the override appears to do nothing. Caught only because a validation instance rendered default text instead of the label that had been set.
flags.handling: Repaired by walking the source and clone trees in lockstep and copying references node-for-node (95 restored). Audited every other set afterwards — Button, Field, Option and Tag were all built by adding properties AFTER combineAsVariants, so none were affected. Recorded in pluginApiNotes.

flags.summary: The notch gap sizer must reproduce every node that widens the visible floating label, not just the label text.
flags.detail: With Required=true the visible notch became [Label][Asterisk] at 81px while the gap slot, sized only by the label text, stayed 72px — so the asterisk sat outside the gap and overlapped the border. Only surfaced on the Error+Required combination.
flags.handling: Added an 'Asterisk sizer' to the Label slot bound to the same Required boolean. Gap now tracks in all four Size x Required combinations (93/93 without, 102/102 with).

flags.summary: The one Tebra-authored TextField element positions itself with a percentage, so its inset scales with field width.
flags.detail: TextFieldOverrides' GrayDownCaretIcon uses right: '4%' and top: calc(50% - 12px). The percentage means a 600px field puts the caret 24px from the edge where a 300px field puts it 12px — Autocomplete's equivalent indicator uses a fixed right: 9. The -12px vertical offset also assumes a 24px icon while fontSize='small' resolves to 20px intended / 22.86px computed.
flags.handling: Transcribed at a fixed 12px inset and vertically centred, with both quirks recorded in the component description.

flags.summary: Naming a TEXT node 'Text' is a no-op, so Figma auto-renames it from its content.
flags.detail: 'Text' is already the default name for a new TEXT node, so assigning it does not clear the node's autoRename flag; the subsequent `characters` assignment overwrites the name. A notch label intended to be called 'Text' came out named 'TextField Label' and broke a name-based lookup. Autocomplete / Field has the same latent inconsistency but was wired by index so it never surfaced.
flags.handling: Set a TEXT node's name AFTER its characters, and never to the literal 'Text'. Recorded in pluginApiNotes.

flags.summary: The Akkurat LL Medium->Bold substitution does not affect any style in the typography.ts ramp.
flags.detail: typography.ts assigns only fontWeight 400 (body1, body2, caption, button) and 700 (h1-h5, subtitle2). Akkurat LL ships Regular and Bold exactly, so the mapping is lossless and no style needed a substitution note. The only place a 500 weight appears is MUI's ListSubheader default (fontWeightMedium), which drives the Autocomplete group label and is not part of the Tebra ramp.
flags.handling: Each style's description states the mapping is exact. The group-label substitution remains recorded on the Autocomplete / Field page notes and in namingFreeze.carriedForward.

flags.summary: LinearEllipsisIcon draws a VERTICAL three-dot stack — a kebab / MoreVert — despite its name.
flags.detail: All three circles share x=12.29 and step down y at 4.29 / 12.0 / 19.71; the path's bounding box is 4.57 wide by 20 tall. The separate EllipsisFilledIcon is the horizontal one (three dots inside a circle).
flags.handling: Named Icon / LinearEllipsis per the library convention (source filename minus the Icon suffix), which traces to source and stays greppable. The appearance/name mismatch is recorded in the component description and flagged for the naming freeze — a designer searching 'kebab' or 'more' will not find it.

flags.summary: MUI sets flexWrap:'wrap' on the Autocomplete inputRoot, so multiple selected values wrap onto extra rows and the field grows.
flags.detail: Confirmed in Autocomplete.js: `[& .inputRoot]: { flexWrap: 'wrap', ... }`. The Figma set models Value=Multiple as one inline row at 56/40.
flags.handling: Accepted modelling simplification — not rebuilt. Recorded in the Autocomplete / Field component description so 56 is not treated as a hard height in dense form compositions.

flags.summary: The chip delete icon is full-strength primary.main because Tebra overrides it — MUI's own default would be a muted 70% (and 26% for filled chips).
flags.detail: MUI Chip gives outlined+coloured chips a deleteIcon at alpha(palette[color].main, 0.7), and filled chips alpha(text.primary, 0.26). ChipOverrides.deleteIcon sets color: theme.palette.primary.main with no alpha, and theme styleOverrides are appended after MUI's base styles, so Tebra wins.
flags.reviewNote: Raised in review as 'should be ~26% muted'. That is the MUI default, not what ships. The saturated teal is a deliberate Tebra override; the glyph and size were the real defects.
flags.handling: Built at full-strength primary.main to match shipped code. If the muted look is wanted, it is a code change in ChipOverrides.deleteIcon, not a Figma correction.

flags.summary: Outlined chips ship a full-strength primary.main border, not MUI's alpha(main, 0.7).
flags.detail: ChipOverrides.outlinedPrimary sets border: 1px solid primary.main and backgroundColor white. MUI's outlined chip is transparent with a 70% border. Both are Tebra overrides that win.
flags.handling: Build confirmed correct — outlined teal chips on white are what the code produces. The ChipOverrides hardcoded hexes (#C3E7C0, #FD919F) live in colorSuccess and colorError and are NOT on the Autocomplete path.

flags.summary: The Autocomplete clear affordance is MUI's internal Close, not Tebra's CloseOutlined.
flags.detail: AutocompleteOverrides.tsx overrides popupIcon only. clearIcon falls through to MUI's default <ClearIcon fontSize='small' />. MUI's Close path spans 5-19 of the 24 viewBox; Tebra's CloseOutlined spans 2-22, so the substituted glyph rendered ~43% larger in the same 20px box.
flags.handling: Icon / Close (MUI) created and swapped in across all 30 Field variants.

flags.summary: Keeping the end adornment in auto-layout flow let the 28px clear indicator inflate field height to 60/44.
flags.detail: In CSS the endAdornment is position:absolute with translateY(-50%), so indicator size can never affect the field box. Only surfaced when Clear icon=true was exercised on an instance — the variant grid defaults it to false and hid the bug.
flags.handling: Adornment is now absolutely positioned and right-pinned; heights verified stable at 56/40 with the clear icon both on and off.

flags.summary: Akkurat LL provides Thin, Light, Regular and Bold — there is no Medium (500) face.
flags.effect: MUI's fontWeightMedium (500), used by ListSubheader for the Autocomplete group label, has no matching font style. In the browser this is synthesised or falls back; in Figma a style must be chosen explicitly.
flags.handling: Group label built at Regular (400) rather than promoted to Bold, and flagged. Do not read the Figma weight as a design decision.

flags.summary: MUI pulls the Button's outer padding in by 4px (2px at small) when a start or end icon is present; Figma cannot vary padding by boolean property.
flags.effect: With an icon toggled on, the Figma component is 4px (2px at small) wider on the icon side than production.
flags.handling: Documented on the Actions page and in geometry.iconPaddingPull. Not faked — the alternative would be doubling the variant matrix to 216.

flags.summary: Figma resolves the component set's defaultVariant to Size=Small regardless of child ordering.
flags.effect: Dragging out an instance yields Small, whereas the code default is Medium (MUI's default size) with color=primary from the theme.
flags.handling: Recorded in the component description and the page notes; the Size option order is left ascending (Small/Medium/Large) rather than reordered to force the default.

flags.summary: StorybookDecorator.tsx wraps stories in ThemeProvider only, with no CssBaseline.
flags.effect: The global :focus-visible outline (0.17.1) and MUI's box-sizing reset never apply in Storybook although they do in the app. Storybook is not a faithful renderer of the shipped result.
flags.handling: Independent confirmation that reading source, not rendering, is the correct method.

flags.summary: packages/billing-system pins @kareo-engineering/design-system 0.6.0 while the workspace package is 0.18.3.
flags.effect: A live consumer frozen one release before the 0.7.0 palette migration — i.e. still on the pre-process palette. Its two stories are not a token source.
flags.handling: Excluded.

flags.summary: ToggleButtonOverrides.ts contains a '&$disabled' rule written in JSS v4 ref syntax. Emotion does not compile it, so the plain disabled state has never received Tebra's treatment.
flags.shipping: MUI's own '&.Mui-disabled': color action.disabled rgba(0,0,0,0.5), border 1px action.disabledBackground rgba(0,0,0,0.12).
flags.note: The neighbouring '&.Mui-selected.Mui-disabled' in the SAME file is written correctly and does execute, so a disabled SELECTED toggle gets grey[400] on white while a disabled UNSELECTED one does not. The two disabled states in one component disagree because of a one-character-class typo.
flags.handling: Built as it ships. Second dead-code finding in the override set after MuiRadioButton; that one was an invalid key, this one is invalid selector syntax, so a key-validity sweep would not have caught it.

flags.summary: Hovering a selected ToggleButton discards Tebra's action.selected #F0EEE8 and renders MUI's computed rgba(0,0,0,0.12) instead.

cascade.tebra: '&.Mui-selected' — specificity (0,2,0), appended after the base so it wins at rest
cascade.mui: '&.Mui-selected:hover' — specificity (0,3,0), which no same-slot override can beat

flags.handling: Both states built as they resolve. Fixing this in code needs the override to carry its own selected:hover rule, exactly as ChipOverrides does for the chip.

flags.summary: SvgIconOverrides.ts's fontSizeSmall / Medium / Large are exact rem restatements of MUI's own pxToRem(20 | 24 | 35) AFTER the 16/14 inflation, so all three are no-ops.
flags.consequence: This is the clearest evidence in the codebase that the pxToRem inflation was transcribed rather than intended: someone read the computed values out of a browser and pasted them back as literals. The file's real content is the three ADDED sizes — fontSizeXxsmall 0.75rem, fontSizeXsmall 1rem, fontSizeSmaller 1.25rem — which are honest px and carry no inflation.
flags.affects: Every icon in every component. Icons encoded as 20 / 24 / 35 render 22.857 / 27.429 / 40. Intended integers are bound in Figma; computedPx recorded per component.
flags.handling: Reported. Nothing rebuilt — the file changes nothing today, but deleting the three restated keys would be a safe no-op cleanup and would make the inflation visible.

flags.summary: AvatarOverrides.ts registers MuiAvatar with defaultProps {} and styleOverrides {} — every rule is commented out. Avatar is 100% substrate.
flags.correction: The coverage sweep classified Avatar as content 'both' and expect 'themed'. That was wrong: the file has a valid key and executes, but contributes nothing.
flags.theTodo: // TODO: handle set sizing and box shadow for disabled elevation — neither half is done. The story passes args { disableElevation: true }, but Avatar has no disableElevation prop, so the arg spreads onto the div and paints nothing. The story is written against an intent that was never implemented.
flags.handling: Built as pure substrate. The empty override and the inert story arg are both recorded in the component description.

flags.summary: ToggleButtonGroupVariations iterates sizes ['large','default','small']. 'default' is not a valid MUI ToggleButton size.
consequences: size='default' matches neither the sizeSmall nor the sizeLarge branch, so the button silently renders MEDIUM padding while carrying a MuiToggleButton-sizeDefault class that styles nothing.

The same string reaches <SvgIcon fontSize='default'>, which indexes MUI's { inherit, small, medium, large } map to undefined and matches no Tebra override either — so that icon has NO font-size rule and falls back to inheriting the button's 16px, instead of the 27.429px a real medium icon would be.

flags.summary: Three ReadMore stories pass isInline where the component prop is $isInline, so the inline behaviour they document never happens.
flags.where: ReadMoreAlert.stories.tsx args, ReadMoreMaxCharacters.stories.tsx args, ReadMoreMaxLines.stories.tsx argTypes.

Story args are assigned as a plain property on the story function and are never checked against ReadMoreProps, so the unprefixed spelling compiles silently. With $isInline undefined, EllipsisText renders display: -webkit-box rather than inline, and the leading space before the button — gated on ($isInline || !isCollapsed) — is skipped too.

flags.summary: ForbiddenErrorMessage links with a raw <a> while its siblings use MUI <Link>, and the package styles no <a> at all, so the two render in different colours.

A raw <a> therefore falls to the user-agent default, conventionally #0000EE with a solid underline, while MUI Link resolves to primary.main #004852 underlined at alpha 0.4. flags.summary: InternalServerErrorMessage ships <Link>contact support</Link> with no href, directly below a TODO saying the link is missing.
flags.where: src/components/Feedback/InternalServerErrorMessage.tsx.

flags.summary: ReadMore asks for color="inherit" but the theme forces primary.main at rest, so "inherit" only takes effect on hover — the label goes from teal to black.
flags.where: src/components/ReadMore/ReadMore.tsx StyledButton, against ButtonOverrides.styleOverrides.text.
flags.detail: MUI sets color: inherit in its base styled() when color="inherit". Tebra ButtonOverrides.text sets color: primary.main and is appended after the base at equal specificity, so the theme wins at rest. StyledButton then adds "&&:hover, &&:active { color: inherit }", whose doubled specificity wins it back on hover. The result is a resting label at #004852 that turns text.primary #000 on hover, over the primary[100] #CBDDE0 hover background the same theme rule supplies.
flags.effect: A colour inversion on hover that nobody appears to have chosen: the component asked for inherit in every state and receives it in exactly one.
flags.handling: Both states to be built as they resolve.

flags.summary: The six Feedback messages share one skeleton and disagree on nearly every measurement in it.

The SVGs declare no width or height of their own, only a viewBox, so an outermost svg stretches to whatever box it is given. flags.detail: 1ch is the advance width of the digit zero in the element own computed font, so 45ch at h2 24px and 75ch at body1 16px are two different pixel values, both dependent on Akkurat LL metrics. Deriving them means reading a font metric rather than a component value; measuring them in a browser is forbidden by the method.

flags.summary: The facesheet card header divider is written as an sx CSS shorthand with a theme path inside it, so the whole declaration is invalid and no divider renders.
flags.where: facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/FacesheetCard.tsx:217 and facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/CardLayout.tsx:170 — the only two occurrences of this pattern in the monorepo.
flags.detail: sx={{ borderBottom: "1px solid background.default", height: "3rem" }}. In sx, a full CSS shorthand string is passed through verbatim; only standalone properties like borderColor resolve theme paths. 'background.default' is not a valid CSS <color>, and an invalid value inside a shorthand invalidates the entire declaration, so border-bottom is dropped rather than falling back to a default colour. The intended colour is background.default = #E8E5DF (Backbone 3).
flags.effect: Two of the eight header bands are the only ones that ask for a divider, and neither draws one. The rendered result is identical to the six clinical-system bands, which makes the divergence invisible in a browser and only findable in source — exactly the case the 'never measure from a rendered component' rule protects against.
flags.fix: borderBottom: 1, borderColor: 'background.default' — or a theme callback: borderBottom: (t) => `1px solid ${t.palette.background.default}`.
flags.handling: Reported, not fixed — web-app-v2 is a read-only reference checkout. Do NOT draw a divider on the Figma band until Daniel decides whether the divider or its absence is the intended design; six of eight sites currently ship without one.

flags.summary: One facesheet card implementation sets CardContent paddingBottom to 128px where its twin sets 16px, because a bare number in sx is a spacing multiple, not pixels.
flags.where: facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/FacesheetCard.tsx:227 vs clinical-system/src/components/Facesheet/Cards/ProblemsCard.tsx:79 (and the five sibling cards).
flags.detail: facesheet-ui writes sx={{ paddingBottom: 16 }}. paddingBottom is in paddingKeys (@mui/system/esm/spacing.js:43), so it routes through createUnaryUnit(theme,'spacing',8,'spacing') (spacing.js:85). theme/theme.ts passes createTheme only palette, typography and components — no spacing key — so createSpacing falls back to its default of 8 (createTheme/createSpacing.js). 16 x 8 = 128px. The clinical-system twins write sx={{ padding: "0 16px 16px 16px" }}, a string, which is taken literally as 16px.
flags.effect: The same card surface has an 8x difference in bottom padding between two live implementations. 128px is almost certainly not intended — the number 16 reads as pixels at a glance, which is how it survived.
flags.handling: Reported. Relevant to Figma only insofar as the card content padding must not be transcribed from facesheet-ui; use the clinical-system 0/16/16/16 values, which match the MUI substrate's 16px.

flags.summary: ImmunizationsCard hardcodes the drawer card style but still renders the fullscreen-only header band, so in fullscreen it is the only facesheet card with no elevation and no min-height.
flags.where: clinical-system/src/components/Facesheet/Cards/ImmunizationsCard.tsx:70 and :71.
flags.detail: Its six siblings wrap in StyledCard (Facesheet.tsx:21-27), which branches on layout: FULLSCREEN gives minHeight 10rem, anything else gives boxShadow none. ImmunizationsCard instead writes <Card sx={DRAWER_CARD_STYLE}> where DRAWER_CARD_STYLE = { boxShadow: 'none' } (types/facesheet.ts:203-205) — unconditionally — and then gates its CardHeader on layout === FacesheetLayout.FULLSCREEN. So in fullscreen it shows the title band on a flat, short card while every sibling is elevated and at least 160px tall.
flags.handling: Reported. Does not change the band spec itself.

flags.summary: Five facesheet cards exist in two live implementations in different packages, and the two disagree on the divider, the content padding and whether the header renders at all.
flags.where: clinical-system/src/components/Facesheet/Cards/* (consumed by FacesheetDrawer.tsx and FacesheetPage.tsx) vs facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/FacesheetCard.tsx (consumed by facesheet-ui CardLayout.tsx).

Which implementation is canonical is a product question. The Figma band should be built once, from the shared geometry (48px, h2/primary, 16px horizontal), with the divider left off until the question is settled.

flags.summary: There is no MuiCardHeader, MuiCardContent or MuiCardMedia override anywhere, so every card-header decision lives in per-site sx.
flags.where: packages/design-system/src/overrides — CardOverrides.ts, CardActionsOverrides.ts and CardActionAreaOverrides.ts are the only Card-family files.

Nothing themes the header. The 48px band, the h2 primary title and the divider are therefore product conventions, not design-system truth.

flags.summary: The partner theme's nav icon hover-colour rule does nothing in five of the six base themes, including Tebra's.
flags.where: design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts MuiIconButton root — '&:hover svg { color: submenuText }' — against baseThemes.ts.

flags.summary: The partner theme silently REPLACES two canonical styleOverrides roots rather than merging with them, because both sides are functions.

flags.summary: The desktop nav bar is 76.8px, not 65px — the inline patient search column is taller than the 65px icon buttons and sets the Toolbar height.

flags.correction: The arithmetic was right and the conclusion was wrong. Superseded by components.PrimaryNavBar.geometryRuling (Daniel, product-rendered authority).

flags.summary: The nav surfaced the first authored-fractional dimensions in the build; resolved by rounding to whole numbers with the computed value recorded.
flags.where: Nav / Bar 1440x76.8, Nav / Search 400x76.8 with a 44.8px field, Nav / Logo 100x23.88, Icon / Payments inner glyph 24x18.24.
flags.detail: Three independent sources, none of them an authoring choice. (1) The 0.3 spacing multiplier in PatientSearch's TextField sx resolves to 2.4px and propagates to 44.8 and 76.8. (2) The Tebra wordmark's viewBox ratio 186.82/782.49 at the declared 100px width gives 23.88. (3) PaymentsIcon's 25x19 viewBox in a 24x24 box gives 18.24. Every previous fractional value in this build was a pxToRem inflation with an intended integer behind it, which the rule handles by binding the integer and recording computedPx. These have no intended integer — the fraction IS the value.

flags.resolution: Daniel, as design authority, ruled on 2026-08-03: round each fractional value to its nearest integer and record the true computed value as computedPx, per the same convention already used for pxToRem inflation. Applied — bar 76.8 -> 77, search column 76.8 -> 77, search field 44.8 -> 45, search text inset 16.4 -> 16, wordmark 23.88 -> 24, Payments glyph 18.24 -> 18 at y 2.88 -> 3. The allDimensionsInteger invariant is restored file-wide. This is recorded as a DESIGNED DECISION (source: Daniel, this pass), not a transcription — the Figma values are deliberately not the computed values, and every departure is documented in the component description and here.
flags.amendment: The standing rule is amended rather than broken: authored-fractional sources get ROUNDED-WITH-RECORD, not preserved. Previously the rule only contemplated pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer existed behind the fraction. It now covers the case where no intended integer exists — the fraction is still not carried into Figma, and computedPx still carries the truth.

standingBatchRules._purpose: Non-negotiable checks every future batch runs before reporting. Added after the paint-opacity defect reached four already-signed-off components.
standingBatchRules.1_instancePaintVerification: Place ONE INSTANCE of every new variant and read its RENDERED paints — colour, effective alpha and bound variable — comparing each against its master. Master-level reads are NOT evidence: paint-level opacity renders correctly on a master and incorrectly on an instance, which is exactly how the defect survived four batches. Any alpha must live in the variable's stored rgba, never as paint-level opacity. SCOPE: that last sentence governs UNBOUND paints only - for a BOUND paint Figma surfaces the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity, and that mirrored value is correct; read rule 9_boundPaintAlpha before touching it.
standingBatchRules.2_unboundPaintAudit: Walk EVERY top-level node on EVERY page, not just component sets. Reference frames, notes frames and loose glyphs count. Auditing only component sets is what let 3 unbound paints sit in the Radio reference frame across several batches.
standingBatchRules.3_referenceCounts: Count componentPropertyReferences per variant after any clone or combineAsVariants — cloning a variant inside a set silently drops them all.
standingBatchRules.4_skipInvisibleFalse: Set figma.skipInvisibleInstanceChildren = false before any audit walk, so boolean-hidden slots are inspected.
standingBatchRules.5_opacityLast: If paint-level opacity is genuinely unavoidable somewhere, apply it as the final operation AND verify on an instance. Prefer promoting to a computed variable.
standingBatchRules.6_enumerateDontRecall: When remediating or sweeping, enumerate from the file rather than from a previously reported list. The alpha remediation's known list was missing 18 of 48 paints.
standingBatchRules.7_fileIdentityFirst: Every Figma call passes fileKey YX2n4YLrEpBXNbcc73T6dw explicitly — never rely on an ambient or last-used file. Every session's FIRST Figma action verifies file identity against this schema's page inventory (figmaBuild.pages._order) before any read informs a decision or any write occurs; if the page list does not match, stop and report rather than proceeding. Added 2026-08-03 after a session read the legacy team library (ZPf0sJy83aPyrHjCVHomya, 'Tebra Working UI Kit') and produced a full reorganisation analysis against the wrong file. Note that figma.root.name returns 'Document' for both files, so the file NAME is not a usable identity check — the page list is.
standingBatchRules.8_roundWithRecord: Never carry a fractional dimension into Figma. Two cases, one treatment. (a) pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer exists behind the fraction: bind the intended integer, record computedPx. (b) Authored-fractional sources, where no intended integer exists — a fractional spacing multiplier, a viewBox ratio, a non-square viewBox in a square box: ROUND to the nearest integer and record the true value as computedPx in both the component description and the schema, and label the rounding a design decision with its source and date. Added 2026-08-03 when the primary nav produced the first case-(b) values (76.8, 44.8, 23.88, 18.24); Daniel ruled round-with-record as design authority. Intrinsic geometry is out of scope for this rule: VECTOR and GROUP bounds are the union of their path data, are not authored, and are not rounded — the tier 6 illustrations already set that precedent.
standingBatchRules.9_boundPaintAlpha: Before changing ANY paint-level opacity, first check whether that paint has a bound colour variable. If it does, Figma SURFACES the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity - it does NOT multiply the two. A paint bound to a variable storing rgba(0,0,0,0.87) correctly reads back paint.opacity 0.87 and renders at 0.87; that is the expected state, not a double-alpha defect, and it must be left alone. Forcing such a paint to opacity 1 DISCARDS the alpha and renders the node fully opaque. Rule 1's 'never as paint-level opacity' applies to UNBOUND paints only. Established empirically 2026-08-26 (checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry) after the opposite assumption produced a real regression on Alert filled/warning; reverted and audited library-wide 2026-08-27 (boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27). To re-confirm at any time: bind a rectangle to an alpha-carrying variable, never set opacity, then read paint.opacity back - it returns the variable's alpha.
standingBatchRules.10_cloneDropsPropertyRefs: Cloning a variant to add a new axis value DROPS componentPropertyReferences on every child. The clone keeps its layers and looks correct, but Label/icon-visibility/icon-swap stop responding — instance property values are stored yet never render, so a swapped instance silently shows the component default. After any variant clone, re-apply refs by copying them from a known-good sibling keyed on child layer name, then verify by reading a nested instance rendered characters against its property value, not just the property value. Hit during buttonInheritColour2026_08_28.
